problems.title: A decreasing logarithm
problems.question: Find the sum of integer roots of log₀.₅(log₂√(x+1))>0.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: For base1/2, the outer inequality means0<log₂√(x+1)<1.
steps: Thus1<√(x+1)<2, or 0<x<3. The integers 1,2 sum to 3.

problems.title: A square root of a logarithm
problems.question: Count integer solutions of √[log₀.₅(x+2)]>1.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: This requires log₀.₅(x+2)>1, or 0<x+2<1/2.
steps: Hence−2<x<−3/2, which contains no integers.

problems.title: Largest logarithmic-inequality solution
problems.question: Find the greatest solution of log₁₀(2x+a)≤0.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
steps: The solution interval is(−a/2,(1−a)/2]. Its right endpoint is included.

problems.title: Cylinder inside a sphere
problems.question: A cylinder has height 3, radius 2 and is inscribed in a sphere. Find sphere radius.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: R²=r²+(h/2)².

problems.title: Axial rectangle from its diagonals
problems.question: A cylinder axial rectangle has diagonal1 and diagonal angle 60°; diameter exceeds height. Find volume.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: Diameter=cos30°=√3/2, height=sin30°=1/2.
steps: Radius=√3/4, so V=πr²h=3π/32.

problems.title: A logarithm with variable base
problems.question: Solve(logₓ(x+1)−2)(2ˣ+3)(|x|+1)>0.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: The domain is x>0, x≠1. The last two factors are positive.
steps: For0<x<1, the logarithm is negative, so no solutions. For x>1, logₓ(x+1)>2 is equivalent to x+1>x².
The positive root of x²−x−1 is(1+√5)/2.

problems.title: Sphere radius from an internal chord
problems.question: An intersection line of two planes is 12 from a sphere centre, and its internal chord is 18. Find sphere volume.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.

problems.title: Count integer radical roots
problems.question: Count integer solutions below8 of √(2x+3)≤x.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: Require x≥0, then square:2x+3≤x², or(x−3)(x+1)≥0.
steps: The valid set is x≥3. Below8, the integers are 3,4,5,6,7.

problems.title: Middle third of a cone
problems.question: A cone axial section is equilateral with side 6. Two parallel planes trisect its height. Find the middle piece volume.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: R=3, h=3√3, V=9√3π. Volumes of similar cones scale as the cube of height.
steps: The middle piece is the difference of cones scaled2/3 and 1/3:V·(8/27−1/27)=7√3π/3.

problems.title: A triangular frustum
problems.question: A regular triangular frustum has lateral edge4 at 60° to its base, and larger base side 4√3. Find volume.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: Height=2√3; vertex horizontal displacement=2. Larger circumradius4, smaller2, so smaller side 2√3.
steps: Base areas are 12√3 and 3√3. V=h(S₁+S₂+√(S₁S₂))/3=(2√3/3)·21√3=42.

problems.title: Factor before solving
problems.question: Count roots of(x²−x)log₂x−2ˣ(x−1)²=(x−1)log₂x.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: The equation factors as(x−1)²(log₂x−2ˣ)=0, x>0.
steps: The second factor is always negative:for 0<x≤1 this is immediate; for x>1, log₂x<x<2ˣ.
Thus the only root is x=1.

problems.title: Possible quadrants of a radical inequality
problems.question: Which quadrants can contain α when√(sinα)≥cosα?
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: The square root requires sinα≥0.
steps: Only quadrants I and II can occur. All quadrant II angles work since cosine is negative; some quadrant I angles work, for example60°.

problems.title: Opposite exponential roots
problems.question: Find a if4ˣ−2^(x+2)+a=0 has two opposite roots.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: Put t=2ˣ>0. Opposite x-values correspond to reciprocal t-values.
steps: The quadratic is t²−4t+a=0. Its reciprocal roots have product 1, so a=1. Its roots 2±√3 are positive and reciprocal, verifying sufficiency.

problems.title: Lateral area of a half-height frustum
problems.question: A pyramid has right isosceles base legs6√2 and all lateral edges6√2. A parallel cut at height midpoint leaves a lower frustum. Find its lateral are a.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: The base hypotenuse is 12. Two lateral faces are equilateral are a 18√3 each; the third is a right isosceles triangle are a 36.
steps: Whole lateral are a=36(√3+1). The small top pyramid has are a scale1/4, so the frustum retains3/4.

problems.title: Orthogonal face diagonals force rhombi
problems.question: An oblique quadrilateral prism has perpendicular diagonals in each lateral face, base diagonals6,8, and lateral edges at 60° to the base. Find volume.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: A parallelogram with perpendicular diagonals is a rhombus. Thus every base side equals the common lateral edge.
steps: The base is a rhombus with side √(3²+4²)=5 and are a 6·8/2=24. Height=5sin60°=5√3/2.

problems.title: A logarithmic identity in x
problems.question: Solve log₁₀((2√3−√2)ˣ)+log₁₀((2√3+√2)ˣ)=x.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: The positive bases multiply to 12−2=10.
steps: The left side is log₁₀(10ˣ)=x for every real x.

problems.title: Joining two identical triangular prisms
problems.question: Two identical right triangular prisms are joined to for m a triangular or quadrilateral right prism. What is the maximum number of different lateral areas?
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: Let triangular base perimeter p, side lengths a, b, c, and prism height h.
steps: Stacking bases gives lateral are a 2ph. Joining across a lateral face on side a, b, or c gives 2h(p−a),2h(p−b), or 2h(p−c).
For a generic scalene triangle these four values differ. These exhaust the full-face joins described.
problems.note: The standard interpretation is that the identical prisms are joined along an entire congruent face.

problems.title: A quadratic in a logarithm
problems.question: Find the product of roots of log₂(16x²)+[log₂(−8x)]²−33=0.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: The domain is x<0. Put t=log₂(−x), giving4+2t+(t+3)²−33=0.
steps: Thus t²+8t−20=0, t=2 or −10. The roots are −4 and −1/1024, and their product is 1/256.

problems.title: Union of two overlapping cones
problems.question: Two congruent cones have equilateral axial sections of side 3, coincident axes and base planes2√3 apart. They overlap. Find union volume.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: Each cone has R=3/2, h=3√3/2, volume9√3π/8. The overlap is two small cones sharing their radius 1/2 base at the midplane, each height √3/2.
steps: Intersection volume=2·π(1/2)²(√3/2)/3=√3π/12.

problems.title: Insphere of a square pyramid
problems.question: A regular square pyramid has height 3 and face apothems at 60° to its base. Find insphere volume.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: Base inradius=3/tan60°=√3, side 2√3; face apothem=3/sin60°=2√3.
steps: Base are a 12, lateral are a 24, total36, and pyramid volume12. For an insphere, r=3V/S=1.
Sphere volume=4π/3.

problems.title: Existence of an exponential-inequality root
problems.question: For which a does a·49ˣ+6·7ˣ−3≥0 have a real solution?
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: Put t=7ˣ>0. For a≥0, the expression at large t is positive.
steps: If a<0, the quadratic maximum on t>0 occurs at t=−3/a and equals −9/a−3. It is nonnegative exactly when a≥−3.
At a=−3, t=1 attains equality.

problems.title: A logarithmic quadratic with at least one solution
problems.question: For which b does(log₃x)²+log₃x+b≥0 have a nonempty solution set?
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: t=log₃x ranges over all real numbers.
steps: For any real b, the quadratic t²+t+b is positive for sufficiently large t. Choose x=3ᵗ.

problems.title: Two cubes stacked inside a cone
problems.question: A cone has right-triangle axial section. A large inscribed cube rests on its base, and a smaller inscribed cube rests on the first. Find the edge ratio.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: The cone has radius equal to height H. For a cube edge s, the radius at its top is H−s, and equals s/√2.
steps: Thus s=H√2/(1+√2). The remaining cone above it has height H−s=H/(1+√2).
The smaller cube is similar with scale1/(1+√2), so large/small edge ratio is 1+√2.

problems.title: Alternate-vertex tetrahedron
problems.question: A rectangular box has volume6. Find the volume of the tetrahedron BA₁C₁D cut out by the stated planes.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: An affine scaling reduces to a unit cube. V_tetra=|det(A₁−B, C₁−B, D−B)|/6.
steps: The determinant magnitude is 2, so this tetrahedron occupies1/3 of the box. Its volume is 6/3=2.
problems.note: The planes specify the usual interior tetrahedron BA₁C₁D; the remaining part of the box would have volume4.

problems.title: A geometric progression from its sum and log sum
problems.question: An increasing positive geometric progression has first-three sum 7 and sum of their base2 logarithms3. Find its third term.
problems.idea: Keep logarithm domains, then reduce to a simple equation or similar solids.
formulas: The product of the three terms is 2³=8, so the middle term is∛8=2.
steps: Write the terms 2/r,2,2r with r>1. Then r+1/r=5/2, so 2r²−5r+2=0 and r=2.
The third term is 4.
